title: status-list-server Helm chart values
description: Configuration values for the status-list-server Helm chart. All top-level blocks are optional; when omitted the chart uses the defaults in values.yaml. The base chart is provider-neutral; cloud-specific behavior (Workload Identity, per-cloud DNS/SecretStore) is enabled through the AWS/GCP/Azure fields documented below.

domain.title: Public DNS suffix
domain.description: Chart-wide public DNS suffix. Leave empty to render localhost/default-neutral hostnames. When set, the default ingress host becomes statuslist.<domain> and the default TLS host becomes *.<domain>. Rendered hostnames are normalized to lowercase.

nameOverride.title: Chart name override
nameOverride.description: Overrides the base chart name used by the _helpers.tpl 'name' / 'fullname' helpers (and therefore resource names and selector labels). Read by the templates; empty uses the chart name (status-list-server).

fullnameOverride.title: Full name override
fullnameOverride.description: Overrides the fully-qualified name (fullname) used for most resource names and the default ServiceAccount when create=true. Read by the _helpers.tpl 'fullname' helper; empty derives <release>-<name>.

serviceAccount.title: Application ServiceAccount
serviceAccount.description: ServiceAccount for the application pods. Attach Workload Identity role annotations here (AWS EKS IRSA eks.amazonaws.com/role-arn, GCP GKE iam.gke.io/gcp-service-account, or Azure AKS azure.workload.identity/client-id) for ambient cloud credentials. The ServiceAccount name defaults to the chart fullname (<release>-status-list-server unless release already contains 'status-list-server', or fullnameOverride if set); the cloud-side trust must be keyed on that name, with the federated subject system:serviceaccount:<namespace>:<name> (IAM role trust for IRSA, roles/iam.workloadIdentityUser binding for GKE, a federated identity credential for AKS — see the env block in values.yaml). Create either chart-managed via create=true or reference an existing one via name.

create.title: Create the ServiceAccount
create.description: create=true renders the ServiceAccount and injects serviceAccountName (chart fullname, or the value of name). create=false with an empty name injects no serviceAccountName, so the pod runs as the namespace default ServiceAccount; set name explicitly when disabling chart SA creation.

name.title: ServiceAccount name
name.description: ServiceAccount name override. Defaults to the chart fullname when create=true (via _helpers.tpl), or to 'default' when create=false with an empty name.

automountServiceAccountToken.title: Mount the Kubernetes API token
automountServiceAccountToken.description: Default false: the application does not need the Kubernetes API, so do not mount the SA bearer token (NSA/CISA hardening, CIS Benchmark 5.1.6). This does NOT break Workload Identity — IRSA / GCP WI / Azure WI use projected OIDC tokens injected by the cloud admission webhook, independent of this setting.

annotations.title: ServiceAccount annotations
annotations.description: Workload Identity role annotations, e.g. eks.amazonaws.com/role-arn (EKS IRSA), iam.gke.io/gcp-service-account (GKE WI), or azure.workload.identity/client-id (AKS WI).

statuslist.title: Application core
statuslist.description: Configuration for the status-list-server Deployment, pods, image, Service, Ingress, runtime environment, secrets, and scaling. The base values are provider-neutral; cloud variants are selected through the image variant and the overlays in helm/README.md.

enabled.title: Deploy the application
enabled.description: Whether to render the application Deployment and its associated resources.

replicaCount.title: Replica count
replicaCount.description: Number of application replicas. Omitted when autoscaling.enabled=true so the HPA controls the replica count.

initContainers.title: Init containers
initContainers.description: Additional init containers. Each is hardened (drop-all capabilities, non-root, read-only rootfs, /tmp emptyDir) and given small fixed CPU/memory requests, so only the image and command need to be supplied. The default waits for the bundled PostgreSQL service.

podLabels.title: Pod labels
podLabels.description: Extra labels merged onto the Pod template metadata. Values are rendered as strings; required e.g. for Azure Workload Identity: azure.workload.identity/use: 'true'.

podAnnotations.title: Pod annotations
podAnnotations.description: Extra annotations merged onto the Pod template metadata (e.g. sidecar injection, monitoring hints), on top of the hard-coded prometheus.io/scrape annotations.

image.title: Application image
image.description: Image reference and selection. Resolution precedence: digest (immutable, repository@digest, pullPolicy IfNotPresent) > tag (mutable, repository:tag, pullPolicy Always) > derived <baseAppVersion>-<variant> (never 'latest'). An empty pullPolicy derives from which resolution is in use.

pullPolicy.title: Image pull policy
pullPolicy.description: IfNotPresent for a digest, Always for a mutable tag. Empty derives from whether a digest is pinned.

variant.title: Image variant suffix
variant.description: Cloud/credential variant suffix applied to the derived tag when neither tag nor digest is set. Selects the credential backend: fscert (filesystem keys/certs), aws, gcp, azure, vault.

tag.title: Image tag
tag.description: Image tag with variant suffix (e.g. 1.2.0-aws). Empty derives <appVersion-without-suffix>-<variant>; never 'latest'.

digest.title: Image digest
digest.description: sha256:<64 hex chars>. Takes precedence over tag, pins the exact digest CI scanned, and defaults pullPolicy to IfNotPresent. Each variant has its own digest; use the digest matching the selected variant.

type.title: Service type
type.description: ClusterIP by default. The chart renders ClusterIP, NodePort, or LoadBalancer; ExternalName is rejected at render time.

annotations.title: Service annotations
annotations.description: Annotations on the Service, e.g. AWS NLB annotations (see values-aws-nlb.yaml).

ingress.title: Ingress
ingress.description: NGINX Ingress exposing the application. The ingressClassName is hard-coded to 'nginx' (ingress.yaml), so 'disable when another controller handles traffic' is the only option — the class is not configurable. The host defaults to statuslist.<global.domain> when set, otherwise localhost. TLS hosts default to *.<global.domain> when global.domain is set, or to the rendered ingress host when secretName is set explicitly.

annotations.title: Ingress annotations
annotations.description: NGINX/cert-manager annotations, e.g. cert-manager.io/cluster-issuer and nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/ssl-redirect.

hosts.title: TLS hosts
hosts.description: Explicit TLS hostnames. Empty defaults to *.<global.domain>, or to the rendered ingress host when secretName is set.

secretName.title: TLS secret name
secretName.description: Empty keeps the neutral default render HTTP-only. Set in overlays that provide TLS material or cert-manager ingress-shim annotations.

externalDnsHostname.title: Explicit ingress hostname
externalDnsHostname.description: Defaults to statuslist.<global.domain> when global.domain is set, otherwise localhost. Rendered lowercase and emitted as an external-dns hostname annotation.

env.title: Application environment variables
env.description: RUNTIME environment for the status-list-server container. APP_DATABASE__PORT is required (the chart fails without it). Do not set APP_DATABASE__URL or APP_DATABASE__PASSWORD here — the chart rejects them (see statuslist.secretMounts and statuslist.fallbackSecret for credential delivery). DNS/Workload Identity settings for ACME DNS-01 are documented in the values.yaml env block and docs/dns-providers.md.

aws.title: AWS application configuration
aws.description: Optional AWS configuration for the application. The chart is provider-neutral by default: serviceAccount.annotations is empty and no credentials are mounted, so you must attach the AWS integration yourself. For IRSA, set the eks.amazonaws.com/role-arn annotation and let the pod-identity webhook inject AWS_ROLE_ARN + AWS_WEB_IDENTITY_TOKEN_FILE (the SDK reads the projected OIDC token; it does NOT use node-instance metadata). Enable mountCredentials only for the legacy static shared-credential-file path.

mountCredentials.title: Mount static AWS credential files
mountCredentials.description: Mounts the resolved aws-credentials-secret into the pod and sets AWS_SHARED_CREDENTIALS_FILE / AWS_CONFIG_FILE. In ESO mode the chart also renders the ExternalSecret that provisions that Secret. Off by default so the base chart stays provider-neutral.

credentialsSecret.title: AWS credentials secret source
credentialsSecret.description: Remote-source layout of the dedicated aws-credentials-secret when mountCredentials=true and externalSecret.enabled.

region.title: AWS region
region.description: Plain (non-secret) AWS region for the application. APP_AWS__REGION is rendered ONLY when secretStore.provider == 'aws' AND an effective region is set (this value, else the legacy secretStore.aws.region fallback — see the status-list-server-chart.appRegion helper). Setting this alone without provider=aws renders nothing; leave both empty and provider=aws for pure-IRSA / Workload Identity installs so the SDK discovers the region from instance metadata.

fallbackSecret.title: Fallback Secret
fallbackSecret.description: Fallback Kubernetes Secret for clusters that do not run External Secrets Operator. Only rendered when externalSecret.enabled=false AND fallbackSecret.enabled=true (the chart fails if both delivery modes are enabled). Always named statuslist-secret; PostgreSQL (postgres.auth.existingSecret) references the same name, so it is deliberately not configurable.

generatedCertificate.title: Generated self-signed certificate
generatedCertificate.description: Local/dev helper for the fscert image that includes a self-signed certificate and signing key. GitOps deployments should not use generated material because helm template runs without cluster lookup and can regenerate values on each sync.

stringData.title: Secret string data
stringData.description: Plain-string Secret values (the API server base64-encodes them). Empty postgres-password means the chart generates a random password and reuses an existing one on upgrades when the cluster is reachable; GitOps tools run helm template without cluster lookup, so provide an explicit password or use ESO.

secretMounts.title: File-based secret mounts
secretMounts.description: Mount Kubernetes Secrets as files into the container (production credential/key rotation, issue #456). fileEnv maps a mounted file path into an application env var; paths are relative to mountPath and must match the mounted items. APP_DATABASE__PASSWORD cannot be delivered any other way: the chart hard-fails if APP_DATABASE__PASSWORD (or APP_DATABASE__URL) is set as a plain env value or fileEnv key, so the mounted APP_DATABASE__PASSWORD_FILE is the only supported database-password delivery path.

fileEnv.title: Environment variable to mounted file mapping
fileEnv.description: Map an env var name to a file path relative to mountPath. Each value must match a mounted items path, be relative, normalized, and resolve inside mountPath (the chart fails otherwise).

watcher.title: Credential rotation watcher
watcher.description: Watcher configuration for file-based credential rotation detection. When pollIntervalSecs is set, APP_WATCHER__POLL_INTERVAL_SECS is injected. Requires an application image implementing the watcher contract (issue #456).

pollIntervalSecs.title: Poll interval
pollIntervalSecs.description: Seconds between file-reload polls; injected as APP_WATCHER__POLL_INTERVAL_SECS.

livenessProbe.title: Liveness probe
livenessProbe.description: httpGet on /health/live (port http). Override the whole block to customize.

readinessProbe.title: Readiness probe
readinessProbe.description: httpGet on /health/ready (port http). Override the whole block to customize.

networkPolicy.title: NetworkPolicy
networkPolicy.description: Opt-in NetworkPolicy (default OFF). When enabled and ingress is empty, a port-only rule allows ANY source in the cluster — you MUST restrict ingress to your ingress controller. Egress always allows 443/53 out to 0.0.0.0/0 (no destination restriction, so outbound exfiltration is not blocked), and scopes PostgreSQL / OTel egress to their labelled pods. statuslist.networkPolicy.egressInternal entries are appended to the PostgreSQL DB-port rule, so they inherit that rule's port — add a matching port when pointing at a different service. This policy does NOT fully isolate the pod on its own.

externalSecret.title: External Secrets Operator mode
externalSecret.description: ESO delivery mode, mutually exclusive with statuslist.fallbackSecret (the chart fails if both are enabled). When enabled the chart renders an ExternalSecret that syncs the application Secret (always named 'statuslist-secret', holder of the database password) from the secret manager referenced by secretStore. With a namespace-scoped SecretStore this requires secretStore.enabled=true or the render fails; only a pre-existing ClusterSecretStore is exempt. Cloud credentials resolve via Workload Identity / IRSA / ManagedIdentity where the provider supports it (Vault token auth and Azure ServicePrincipal + authSecretRef use static secrets instead). The ExternalSecret target name is intentionally not configurable and fails at render time if changed.

secretStoreRef.title: SecretStore reference
secretStoreRef.description: References a namespace SecretStore (rendered by this chart) or a pre-existing cluster-scoped ClusterSecretStore (not rendered here).

name.title: Target secret name
name.description: Single supported application-secret name shared with the Deployment, PostgreSQL, and the fallback Secret. Any other value fails at render time; intentionally not configurable.

creationPolicy.title: Creation policy
creationPolicy.description: Per the upstream External Secrets Operator CreationPolicy: Owner | Orphan | Merge | None | CreateOrMerge. Orphan leaves an existing target Secret in place for Argo pruning to keep deleting; CreateOrMerge merges only on create.

data.title: Remote secret data
data.description: Mappings of secretKey (local) to remoteRef (remote key/property). The default maps postgres-password from the POSTGRES_PASSWORD property of the 'statuslist-secret' remote key.

extraExternalSecrets.title: Additional ExternalSecrets
extraExternalSecrets.description: Optional additional ExternalSecret resources for separately mounted Secrets (file-based database credentials, token signing keys, API keys). Each renders its own ExternalSecret and may override refreshInterval and secretStoreRef; defaults come from externalSecret.spec.

secretStore.title: ESO SecretStore / ClusterSecretStore
secretStore.description: SecretStore reference that externalSecret syncs from, selecting the cloud or on-prem secret manager. Rendered only when externalSecret.enabled AND secretStore.enabled, and only for a namespace-scoped SecretStore; a ClusterSecretStore kind is expected to pre-exist cluster-wide and is not rendered. Provider auth is decoupled from the application's own Workload Identity where noted.

provider.title: Provider selector
provider.description: Secret provider: aws (Secrets Manager / Parameter Store), vault (HashiCorp Vault / OpenBao), gcp (GCPSM), azure (Azure Key Vault), raw (full ESO provider body passthrough). Required when enabled=true.

region.title: AWS region
region.description: Region for the ESO AWS SecretStore. Setting it here is the legacy fallback: when statuslist.aws.region is empty AND secretStore.provider == 'aws', this value is injected as APP_AWS__REGION (see the status-list-server-chart.appRegion helper). It is NOT 'opt-in / not injected' — set it only if you want the pod's region pinned. Leave both regions empty and provider='aws' with a wildcard/IRSA role to let the SDK discover the region from instance metadata. The ESO AWS SecretStore itself still needs a concrete region and falls back to eu-central-1 at the CR level when both values are empty, so a cluster in another region without an explicit region gets a real SecretSyncedError — treat eu-central-1 as an effective default, not a formality.

authType.title: Azure auth type
authType.description: Per the External Secrets Operator AzureKVProvider CRD: ServicePrincipal | ManagedIdentity | WorkloadIdentity. ManagedIdentity uses identityId; ServicePrincipal client credentials go under authSecretRef. 'ClientSecret' is not a valid CRD value and is rejected.

serviceAccountRef.title: ESO ServiceAccount reference
serviceAccountRef.description: References the External Secrets Operator controller's own ServiceAccount (least privilege), not the application ServiceAccount. namespace should match the ESO controller namespace; leave empty when ESO is in this release namespace.

raw.title: Raw ESO provider passthrough
raw.description: Full ESO provider spec passthrough for unsupported providers (secretStore.provider=raw). Holds ONLY the concrete provider body rendered directly under spec.provider (no extra top-level 'provider' key), e.g. { webhook: { url: '...' } }. Render-time validation rejects an empty/raw-only object to avoid emitting an insecure SecretStore.

postgres.title: Bundled PostgreSQL
postgres.description: Bundled in-cluster PostgreSQL (accepted values of the CloudPirates chart). One possible backend: the application is database-agnostic and selects its backend at runtime via APP_DATABASE__* env vars. Set enabled=false and point APP_DATABASE__* at an external database for a different backend. Note: only the PostgreSQL backend is delivered by this chart — no MySQL (or other) image variant is published, so 'including MySQL' applies to the application code only, not to a Helm-installable MySQL. If you disable postgres, you must also override statuslist.initContainers (the default wait-for-postgres init container otherwise hangs on <release>-postgres) and add egress for your external database host.

existingSecret.title: Existing secret name
existingSecret.description: Must reference the same secret the application reads (statuslist-secret, see the status-list-server-chart.appSecretName helper). Fixed to statuslist-secret in both modes: fallback mode renders that exact name, and ESO mode rejects any externalSecret.spec.target.name other than it at render time — there is nothing to keep in sync.

storageClass.title: Storage class
storageClass.description: Empty string uses the cluster default StorageClass.

autoscaling.title: HorizontalPodAutoscaler
autoscaling.description: HPA (autoscaling/v2). When enabled the Deployment omits replicas so the HPA controls the count. Scaled pods share the application ServiceAccount; each gets its own short-lived Workload Identity token, so no per-pod cloud registration is required. minReplicas > maxReplicas is rejected at render time.

podDisruptionBudget.title: PodDisruptionBudget
podDisruptionBudget.description: PDB (policy/v1). Use with replicaCount > 1 / HPA so disruption events keep the minimum replicas available. Set exactly one of minAvailable / maxUnavailable; the chart rejects both set or neither set. minAvailable must be < replica count (or autoscaling.minReplicas) or voluntary evictions are blocked; the safe default is maxUnavailable: 1. An explicit 0 is preserved.

serviceMonitor.title: ServiceMonitor
serviceMonitor.description: ServiceMonitor (monitoring.coreos.com/v1) for kube-prometheus-stack / Prometheus Operator discovery. Prometheus deployments driven by the Operator discover scrape targets through ServiceMonitor CRs rather than prometheus.io/* annotations; enable to define the /metrics endpoint on the application Service.

labels.title: ServiceMonitor labels
labels.description: Selector labels required by your Prometheus ServiceMonitorSelector, e.g. release: kube-prometheus-stack.

interval.title: Scrape interval
interval.description: e.g. '15s'. Empty uses the Operator default.

scrapeTimeout.title: Scrape timeout
scrapeTimeout.description: e.g. '10s'. Empty uses the Operator default.

prometheusRule.title: PrometheusRule
prometheusRule.description: PrometheusRule (monitoring.coreos.com/v1) shipping the SLI recording rules and SLO burn-rate / error-budget alerting rules as a single CRD. Alert thresholds come from the slo block. Only the values.yaml slo.* defaults are checked against deploy/observability/slo/thresholds.json and the standalone deploy/observability/prometheus/rules/*.rules.yml by lint-thresholds.mjs; the hard-coded alert summary strings inside this template are not covered by that lint.

labels.title: PrometheusRule labels
labels.description: Selector labels required by your Prometheus RuleSelector, e.g. release: kube-prometheus-stack.

slo.title: SLO thresholds
slo.description: SLO target thresholds consumed by the prometheusrule template (prometheusrule.yaml) to build SLI recording rules and SLO burn-rate / error-budget alerting rules. Values are accepted as either JSON numbers or numeric strings — helm's --set passes floats as strings, so a number-only type would reject --set slo.errorRateTarget=0.004 (use --set-json or a values file for full parity; --set works for these). The values.yaml slo.* defaults are asserted against deploy/observability/slo/thresholds.json and the standalone deploy/observability/prometheus/rules/*.rules.yml by lint-thresholds.mjs; the summary strings inside prometheusrule.yaml are NOT covered by that lint and are hard-coded.

errorRateTarget.title: Error-rate SLO target
errorRateTarget.description: Acceptable ratio of 5xx to all requests over the SLO window (0.005 = 0.5%). Multiplicand of the burn-rate thresholds (threshold = errorRateTarget x multiplier) and denominator of the error-budget success ratio. Note: also drives the token-generation burn-rate and budget alerts.

fastBurnMultiplier.title: Fast-burn multiplier
fastBurnMultiplier.description: Fast-burn alert threshold = errorRateTarget x this (14.4x), evaluated on the 1h and 5m windows for 5m. Pages.

slowBurnMultiplier.title: Slow-burn multiplier
slowBurnMultiplier.description: Slow-burn alert threshold = errorRateTarget x this (6.0x), evaluated on the 6h and 30m windows for 30m. Warns.

requestLatencyP95.title: Request latency P95 target (s)
requestLatencyP95.description: P95 request latency target in seconds (0.3 = 300ms). Exceeding on the fast or slow burn windows fires an alert.

dbLatencyP95.title: DB latency P95 target (s)
dbLatencyP95.description: P95 database query latency target in seconds (0.05 = 50ms). Same fast/slow burn semantics.

cacheHitRatioMin.title: Minimum cache hit ratio
cacheHitRatioMin.description: Minimum acceptable status-list cache hit ratio (0.85 = 85%); below this for 15m fires a warn.

certRenewalFailureMax.title: Max certificate-renewal failure ratio
certRenewalFailureMax.description: Accepted for parity with the standalone rules and thresholds.json, but NOT consumed by prometheusrule.yaml — this chart's cert alert is expiry-driven (certExpiryWarnSeconds / certExpiryCriticalSeconds); tuning this value has no effect here.

errorBudgetCriticalThreshold.title: Error-budget critical threshold
errorBudgetCriticalThreshold.description: Remaining-error-budget gate for the ErrorBudget*Critical page alerts; below this fraction of the 30d budget remaining pages.

certExpiryWarnSeconds.title: Certificate expiry warn seconds
certExpiryWarnSeconds.description: Seconds remaining that trigger a warn (1209600 = 14d). Cert renewal is a discrete low-frequency event, so alerts watch the continuous cert_time_to_expiry_seconds gauge.

certExpiryCriticalSeconds.title: Certificate expiry critical seconds
certExpiryCriticalSeconds.description: Seconds remaining that trigger a page (604800 = 7d).

alerting.title: AlertmanagerConfig alerting
alerting.description: AlertmanagerConfig (monitoring.coreos.com/v1beta1) routing SLO alerts to a notification channel — the Kubernetes equivalent of the Docker Compose ALERTMANAGER_PLATFORM + generate-alertmanager-config.sh setup. Supported platforms: discord, slack, teams, mattermost, webhook (via alerting.webhookUrl) and email (via alerting.email.*). Route tree: severity=none -> deadmansswitch, severity=page -> human (repeat 4h), severity=warn -> human (repeat 24h), everything else -> noop.

platform.title: Notification platform
platform.description: Platform selector, must match one of the supported values above.

dashboardUrl.title: Dashboard URL
dashboardUrl.description: Grafana dashboard URL injected into alert annotations.

slack.title: Slack channel override
slack.description: Optional Slack channel override (e.g. '#alerts'). Leave empty to use the webhook default channel.

labels.title: AlertmanagerConfig labels
labels.description: Additional labels required by your Alertmanager selector (e.g. release).

existingSecret.title: Pre-existing credentials secret
existingSecret.description: Name of a pre-existing Secret containing credentials. When set the chart does NOT render its own Secret (recommended for production); the Secret must already exist and contain the platform keys (webhook-url, optional dms-webhook-url / smtp-password).

webhookUrl.title: Webhook URL
webhookUrl.description: Inline webhook URL for discord/slack/teams/mattermost/webhook. Never commit real tokens — use existingSecret + ESO/Vault in production.

dmsWebhookUrl.title: Dead-man's-switch URL
dmsWebhookUrl.description: The always-firing Watchdog pings this so a collapsed pipeline is detected by its ABSENCE. Empty absorbs the Watchdog.

dmsEnabled.title: Enable Dead Man's Switch
dmsEnabled.description: Enable DMS when using existingSecret (reads key dms-webhook-url). When dmsWebhookUrl is set, DMS is enabled implicitly.

webhookTimeout.title: Webhook timeout
webhookTimeout.description: Per-request timeout for webhook/Teams/Mattermost/DMS receivers as a Go duration string (e.g. '10s').

email.title: Email settings
email.description: Email settings (required only when platform=email). to/from/smarthost render as plain CRD strings; only the optional SMTP password is read from the Secret (smtp-password).

smtpPassword.title: SMTP AUTH password
smtpPassword.description: Stored in the alerting Secret as smtp-password (or read from existingSecret) and referenced via authPassword. Empty disables SMTP AUTH.

tlsConfig.title: Email TLS config
tlsConfig.description: EmailConfig tlsConfig overrides (certificate handling). Empty disables custom TLS settings.

opentelemetry-collector.title: OpenTelemetry Collector subchart
opentelemetry-collector.description: OpenTelemetry Collector subchart (opentelemetry-collector dependency). When enabled the Deployment injects APP_TELEMETRY__ENABLED=true and APP_TELEMETRY__OTLP_ENDPOINT pointing at the collector Service, and network-policy.yaml opens OTLP egress. The default config uses the dev-only debug exporter; configure production exporters in config.exporters.
